title: Invariants and Edge Cases Check
description: Spot empty-input bugs and invariant thinking.

questions.prompt: What’s wrong with `let m = arr[0]` max on some inputs?

options.text: Empty array makes `arr[0]` undefined and the loop may not run

questions.explanation: Empty input is the common silent bug: `arr[0]` is `undefined`; loops may not run. Guard empty before assuming a first element.

options.text: True only before the first iteration
A fact that stays true as the loop runs (checkable after iterations)
Identical to the function’s return type
Optional documentation with no relation to correctness

questions.explanation: Invariants are facts that stay true as the loop runs. An invariant should be checkable after every iteration — good for debugging.

questions.prompt: Which edge cases should you list before coding?

options.text: Only the happy path with many distinct values
Empty, single element, duplicates, all equal, sorted / reverse sorted

questions.explanation: List empty, single element, duplicates, all equal, and sorted / reverse sorted — they break naive assumptions.

options.text: They change binary-search bounds and sort stability concerns

questions.explanation: Duplicates are not noise; they change binary-search bounds and sort stability.
